https://www.politico.eu/article/emma-bon.text: Italian liberal politician Emma Bonino died Friday at the age of 78 , prompting tributes from across the political spectrum for the civil-rights activist and former European commissioner. “Emma Bonino has represented for decades a strong and recognizable voice of Italian politics, carrying forward her ideas with determination,” said Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni , an ideological foe about whom Bonino was fiercely critical during the 2022 election campaign. “Our stories and our sensibilities have been distant, yet this has never prevented me from recognizing their weight and role in the public life of our nation,” Meloni, who leads the right-wing Brothers of Italy party, added. Advertisement Advertisement A veteran of Italy’s fight for civil and women’s rights, Bonino played a key role in the campaigns that led to the legalization of divorce and abortion in the country during the 1970s. In 2017, she co-founded the liberal More Europe party, which paid tribute to her on Friday. “Activist, parliamentarian, minister, European commissioner. Always radically free,” party leader Riccardo Magi wrote on X . “Her life was a long struggle against everything that denies freedoms.” Carlo Calenda, leader of the liberal Italian Action party, said : “The last great protagonist of the civil battles that led to the modernization of this country,” adding that “a piece of Italian and European political history is passing away.” Bonino’s endeavors extended beyond Italy. She served as a European commissioner in the 1990s, notably overseeing an increase in humanitarian aid to countries and regions affected by some of the most devastating conflicts of the decade, including the Balkans, Rwanda and Afghanistan. “Emma Bonino has never waited for the world to be ready. She has always chosen to move forward, showing the way to others,” wrote European Parliament President Roberta Metsola . “The Europe she fought for will miss her.”

Photograph: Patricia Pinto/Reuters Bolivia Bolivia investigates ex-president Evo Morales over alleged ties to 2009 killings Leftist former leader accused of involvement in shooting of three Europeans in Santa Cruz and torture of two others AFP Mon 12 Oct 2026 17.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Bolivia’s attorney general has announced an investigation into leftist former president Evo Morales , alleging his involvement in the murder and torture of European citizens in 2009. Seventeen years ago, police raided a hotel in the city of Santa Cruz, shooting dead Eduardo Rózsa Flores, a Bolivian-Croatian, Michael Dwyer, an Irishman, and Árpád Magyarosi, a Hungarian-Romanian. Bolivian-Croatian citizen Mario Tadic and Elöd Tóásó from Hungary survived and reported being tortured after their arrest. The Morales administration in power at the time claimed that Rózsa Flores was leading efforts to promote a separatist movement, with funding from the rightwing economic elite of Santa Cruz. Bolivia rocked by protests as US warns of ‘coup d’état’ Read more Acting attorney general José Armando Urioste announced the preliminary investigation into Morales just one week into the job on Monday. In a letter to the supreme court, Urioste said authorities were gathering evidence against Morales and his former vice-president Álvaro García Linera “for the alleged commission of the crimes of murder, abuse, torture and unlawful detention”. The investigation comes after a complaint filed by rightwing lawmakers Tomasa Yarhui and Rodrigo Antonio. When the raid occurred, Morales told the press during an official visit to Venezuela that he had ordered the detention of the foreigners, whom he called “mercenaries”. Family members and victims brought the case before the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, which concluded in 2021 that the government had violated human rights. Neither of the accused has commented on the latest inquiry. Morales, the first-ever Indigenous person to lead Bolivia, is currently in hiding from two active arrest warrants against him. One relates to his alleged role in massive protests that paralysed the country for 53 days earlier this year. The other accuses him of trafficking a minor with whom he is said to have had a daughter. Morales denies the allegations.
